title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 51
paragraphs: The generals in council with one another resolved that, if the Persians put off the battle for that day, they would go to the Island. This is ten furlongs from the Asopos and the spring Gargaphia where they were then encamped, and lies in front of the Plataeans' city. And if it be asked how there can be an island on the mainland, here is how: the river parts in two upstream, flowing from Kithairon down into the plain, with about three furlongs between its streams, and then joins again into one; its name is Oëroe, said by the natives to be the daughter of Asopos. To this place, I say, they decided to move so that they might have an abundant water supply and not be damaged by the cavalry, as they now were while they stood directly opposite. They proposed to make the move when the second watch of the night had come, so that the Persians might not see them set out and harass them with the cavalry in pursuit. They also planned, after arriving at this place — around which, as I say, Oëroe the daughter of Asopos flows, parting into two streams as she runs down from Kithairon — to send half the army to Kithairon during that same night to pick up the attendants who had gone for provisions, since those were cut off from them in Kithairon.
